title: Steak au Poivre with Crispy Potatoes & Vegetable Sides
summary: Grilled filet mignon with a brandy, cream and green-peppercorn sauce, crispy roasted potatoes, honey-thyme carrots, Parmesan cauliflower and steam-charred green beans. Brian demonstrates the full meal workflow, but supplies no serving count or measured ingredient quantities.

ingredients.note: For boiling the potatoes; not a measured quantity.
Added after draining and drizzled over the tray. No measured amount is supplied.

steps.text: Peel, cube and rinse the potatoes. Add a healthy amount of salt and fresh thyme, then bring to a boil. Brian starts these first because they take the longest.
Once fully cooked, drain, add a bit of olive oil and toss so a rough mashed-potato crust forms on the pieces.

Gently transfer to a sheet pan, drizzle with olive oil and put in the oven at 400 °F. This is the method actually used; Brian says he normally uses a preheated pan with more oil but did not have enough olive oil for that version.
When a crispy crust has developed, turn the potatoes individually so the other sides crisp as well. No total roasting time is supplied.
Peel the carrots, or scrub them clean as Brian's stated alternative. Drizzle with olive oil, add salt and honey, rub all over, and add a few sprigs of thyme.
Wrap tightly in foil and put in the oven to steam in their own juices. A carrot-specific temperature and cooking time are not stated.
Once sweet and tender, open the foil and return the carrots to the oven uncovered to roast and caramelize.

ingredients.note: Brown sugar specifically; the existing sugar filter key is reused.

steps.text: Trim into roughly equal-sized florets, rinse and drain. Coat in olive oil and season with smoked paprika, salt, garlic powder, onion powder and a little brown sugar.
Put in the oven to char. Give the cauliflower a mix during roasting so it cooks evenly, then return it to the oven. A cauliflower-specific temperature and roasting time are not stated.
When nearly done, grate fresh Parmesan over the cauliflower and return to the oven until the cheese crisps onto it.

ingredients.note: Brian explicitly chooses green peppercorns rather than black pepper. No separate addition of the brine is specified.
Already reduced when added. No stock recipe or reduction ratio is supplied; beef stock is not silently substituted.
Intended for finishing the sauce; Brian forgets and uses them on top of the plated steaks instead.

steps.text: Finely mince the shallots and sweat them in melted butter with minced garlic.
Chop the green peppercorns in brine and add to the pot. Mix, deglaze with brandy and let it reduce.
Once the harsh alcohol smell of the brandy is gone, add heavy cream and reduced veal stock, then reduce further. Brian gives no quantities, reduction ratio or duration.
Finely slice the chives without bruising them. Brian intends to finish the sauce with them but actually adds them on top of the plated steaks.

ingredients.note: Oil type is not identified in the narration.

steps.text: Line up and trim off the tough stem ends. Cut the beans in half for easier eating, rinse and let them dry for a bit.
Put the beans into a saucier with a little oil, water and salt. Cover over high heat and steam.
After a few minutes, remove the lid. As the water evaporates, let the green beans pick up a little char in the oil.

ingredients.note: Brian says he seasoned heavily the night before, without identifying the seasoning. Salt and black pepper are not inferred.
Oil type is not identified in the narration.

steps.text: Season the steaks heavily the night before, as Brian says he did. The seasoning ingredients, steak count, weight and thickness are not supplied.

Coat the steaks in a little oil and grill. The video does not state grill temperature, time per side or a target internal temperature; the guests arriving in ten minutes is not a cooking-time instruction.
Let the steaks rest for a few minutes before plating.

Serve the sauce on the side, as for Brian's clients, or spoon it underneath the steak, as for the guests. Add the cauliflower, carrots, potatoes, green beans and steak; scatter the sliced chives over the steak as shown.

notes: The complete publicly narrated workflow is captured, so this is marked analyzed; it is not a fully measured recipe. No ingredient weights, exact serving count or nutrition are supplied.

The source describes a private-chef lunch in Beverly Hills and makes vegetable/pesticide and nutrition-related comments. Those claims are not independently verified or needed for the cooking instructions.
